name: Netflix
cancelSteps: Sign in at netflix.com
Go to the Manage your membership page (netflix.com/cancelplan)
Click Cancel
Click Finish Cancellation to confirm
traps: Signing out or deleting the app does not cancel the account; you must complete the cancelplan flow
If someone restarts the account after you cancel, billing resumes
refundBasis: Netflix's terms state payments are nonrefundable and there are no refunds or credits for partial-month membership periods.

name: Hulu
cancelSteps: Sign in at secure.hulu.com/account (no single cancel-link exists; use the Account page)
Find Your Subscription section and select Cancel
Skip the pause offer if shown and choose Continue to Cancel
Select Cancel Subscription to confirm
traps: Canceling Hulu does not delete the underlying Disney account used for other Disney services
If billed through a third party (e.g. a cable/carrier bundle), cancellation must happen with that third party instead
refundBasis: Hulu's terms say it does not refund or credit for partially used subscription terms or billing periods, except as required by law or at its sole discretion.

name: Disney+
cancelSteps: Sign in at disneyplus.com/account (no single cancel-link exists; use the Account page)
Go to Your Plans & Billing
Select Cancel Subscription and follow the prompts
traps: If you subscribed through Apple, Google, or Amazon, Disney+ cannot cancel it for you — you must cancel with that platform
Cancelling forfeits unused service, referral, or gift-card credits
refundBasis: The Disney+ Subscriber Agreement states there are no refunds or credits for partially used billing periods, except at Disney's sole discretion or as required by law.

name: HBO Max
cancelSteps: Sign in at hbomax.com/subscription
Select Cancel Your Subscription
Confirm; note the expiration date shown
traps: Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription — it auto-renews until cancelled through the correct biller
If billed through Amazon, Apple, Google Play, Roku, or a carrier, cancellation must happen there instead (check the biller first)
refundBasis: HBO Max's help center only documents a prorated refund for Extra Member Add-Ons; no general refund policy for the base plan is published.

name: Paramount+
cancelSteps: Sign in at paramountplus.com/account
Click your username, then Account
Scroll to Subscription & Billing and select Cancel Subscription
Click Continue to Cancel and confirm
traps: If subscribed via Apple, Google, or Amazon, cancel through that platform instead
refundBasis: Paramount+ support states you keep access until the billing period ends but will not be refunded for fees already paid.

name: Peacock
cancelSteps: Log in at peacocktv.com/account/plans
Select Cancel All Subscriptions to remove the base plan and any add-ons
Confirm cancellation; a confirmation email is sent
traps: If subscribed through Apple, Amazon, Google, Roku, or another platform, Peacock cannot cancel it — you must cancel with that third party
refundBasis: Peacock's help article states no refunds or credits will be issued for prior payments when you cancel or downgrade, unless required by law.

name: YouTube Premium
cancelSteps: Go to youtube.com/paid_memberships and sign in
Click Deactivate next to the membership
Click Continue to cancel
Choose a reason, click Next, then click Yes, cancel
traps: If purchased through the iOS App Store, you must cancel via Apple's Subscriptions settings instead
refundBasis: Google's help article for cancelling YouTube Premium does not state a refund policy for the membership itself.

name: YouTube TV
cancelSteps: Go to tv.youtube.com on a web browser and sign in
Select your profile photo, then Settings
Select Membership, then Manage
Click Cancel membership
traps: If subscribed through a mobile carrier or internet provider, YouTube TV cannot refund you — that provider's policy applies instead
refundBasis: Google states YouTube TV does not give refunds or credits for partial billing periods; refunds are only considered if a feature is defective.

name: Spotify
cancelSteps: Sign in at spotify.com/account
Under Subscription, select Manage your subscription
Select Cancel Subscription and confirm
traps: If billed through Apple or Google, cancel via that app store's subscription settings instead
Cancelling does not refund the current billing period — Premium stays active until the next billing date
refundBasis: Spotify says cancelling does not refund a payment already processed; a refund right exists only within 14 days of a purchase and is void once the service is used.

name: Apple (App Store / iCloud+ / Apple One)
cancelSteps: On iPhone/iPad: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > select the subscription > Cancel Subscription
On Mac: App Store > your name > Account Settings > Subscriptions > Manage > select subscription > Cancel Subscription
Without an Apple device: sign in at account.apple.com and manage Subscriptions there
Cancellation applies to any app or service billed through Apple, not just Apple's own apps
traps: This is the required path for ANY app subscription bought through the iOS/Mac App Store, even if the app itself is a different company's product
Refunds for Apple purchases are requested separately at reportaproblem.apple.com, not guaranteed
refundBasis: Apple accepts refund requests via reportaproblem.apple.com for recent charges, though approval is case-by-case.

name: Google Play Subscriptions
cancelSteps: Go to play.google.com/store/account/subscriptions and sign in
Select the subscription to cancel
Click Cancel subscription and confirm
On Android: Play Store app > profile icon > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions
traps: This is the required path for ANY app subscription bought through Google Play, even if the app itself is a different company's product
Uninstalling the app does not cancel the subscription
refundBasis: Google Play accepts refund requests through its own refund flow, though approval is discretionary and generally time-limited.

name: Amazon Prime
cancelSteps: Sign in and go to Your Memberships and Subscriptions
Find Prime, select Manage Subscription
Select Cancel Subscription under Advanced Controls
Confirm the end date
traps: If Prime was signed up for via Google Play/Android, cancel through Google's subscription settings instead
refundBasis: Amazon states paid members who haven't used Prime benefits are eligible for a full refund of the current membership period, processed in three to five business days.

name: Audible
cancelSteps: Sign in at audible.com
Select your name in the top navigation, then Membership details
Select the Cancel membership link
If billed through the App Store or Google Play, follow that platform's cancellation steps instead
traps: Titles purchased with credits remain yours to keep after cancellation, but the membership itself is not refunded
refundBasis: Audible says cancelling does not refund fees already paid, though an unused monthly credit may sometimes be pro-rated depending on timing.

name: Kindle Unlimited
cancelSteps: Sign in and go to Your Memberships and Subscriptions
Find Kindle Unlimited membership settings
Select Cancel Kindle Unlimited Membership, then Cancel Membership
traps: Checked-out books become unavailable once access ends after the billing date
refundBasis: Amazon's Kindle Unlimited help page covers cancellation steps but does not state a refund policy.

name: Microsoft 365
cancelSteps: Sign in at account.microsoft.com/services/microsoft365 with the account used to purchase
Select Cancel subscription
Follow the prompts to confirm
traps: If purchased via Google Play, the Apple App Store, or a third-party retailer, you must cancel and get refunds through them instead
refundBasis: Microsoft offers a prorated refund within 7 days of a charge for MCA billing accounts, or a prorated credit/refund for MOSA accounts; policy varies by billing type and country.

name: Xbox Game Pass
cancelSteps: Sign in at account.microsoft.com/services with the Microsoft account used for Game Pass
Under Services & subscriptions, select Manage next to the Game Pass subscription
Select Cancel subscription and confirm
traps: Cancelling revokes access to the entire Game Pass library, including titles you had installed
refundBasis: Xbox subscriptions fall under Microsoft's general subscription refund policy, which allows a prorated refund/credit shortly after a charge depending on billing account type and country.

name: Adobe Creative Cloud
cancelSteps: Sign in at account.adobe.com
Select Manage plan for the plan you want to cancel
Follow the prompts to confirm cancellation
traps: Cancelling an annual plan (paid monthly) after 14 days triggers an early-termination fee of 50% of the remaining contract balance
If purchased via Apple, Google, or Microsoft, Adobe can't cancel it — cancel through that provider instead
refundBasis: Adobe gives a full refund if you cancel within 14 days of the initial purchase; after that, payments are non-refundable and annual plans incur a termination fee.

name: Dropbox
cancelSteps: Sign in at dropbox.com/account/plan
Select the option to downgrade/cancel the paid plan
Confirm; the account converts to free Dropbox Basic at the end of the billing cycle
traps: Dropbox also accepts cancellation by physical mail letter if you can't cancel online
refundBasis: Dropbox says it generally doesn't issue refunds for US customers; a 14-day refund right applies only to subscribers in the EU, UK, or Turkey.

name: Norton
cancelSteps: Log in at my.norton.com
Select Manage my subscriptions
Choose the option to cancel/turn off auto-renewal
Uninstall the software from your devices after cancelling
refundBasis: Norton offers a 60-day money-back guarantee on annual subscriptions (each renewal charge included) and a 14-day guarantee on monthly subscriptions.

name: McAfee
cancelSteps: Sign in at myaccount.mcafee.com
Select Account, then Auto-Renewal Settings
Select Update settings for the subscription, then End my membership
Click through the retention offer screen — cancellation isn't final until you do
traps: McAfee shows a retention offer ("Before you go") after you click cancel; the subscription is not actually cancelled until you click past it
Apple- and Google-billed subscriptions must be cancelled through those stores
refundBasis: McAfee offers a full refund within 30 days of an initial purchase or within 60 days of an automatic-renewal charge for eligible direct consumer purchases.

name: Avast
cancelSteps: Sign in at id.avast.com
Go to My account, then Order History
Select Request a Refund on the eligible order (which also stops the subscription), or use My subscriptions > Manage subscriptions to turn off renewal
refundBasis: Avast offers a 30-day money-back guarantee for purchases made directly through Avast, the Avast app, or Google Play.

name: AVG
cancelSteps: Sign in at my.avg.com with the email used to purchase
Click Manage subscriptions on the My subscriptions tile
Select the subscription and turn off automatic renewal
traps: The money-back guarantee does not apply to AVG purchased from retail stores or third-party resellers — contact them instead
refundBasis: AVG offers a 30-day money-back guarantee for purchases made directly through the AVG website or Google Play.

name: Malwarebytes
cancelSteps: Sign in at my.malwarebytes.com
Go to the payment page for the subscription
Click Turn auto-renewal off, select a reason, and click Send
traps: Android/iOS subscriptions must be cancelled through Google Play or the Apple App Store instead
refundBasis: Malwarebytes offers a 60-day money-back guarantee for direct Online Store purchases and renewals.

name: LinkedIn Premium
cancelSteps: Sign in and go to the My Premium page (linkedin.com/premium)
Open Manage Premium account settings
Select Cancel subscription and confirm
Cancel at least 1 day before the next billing date to avoid another charge
traps: If purchased via iTunes/App Store, cancellation starts on LinkedIn but finishes in Apple's Subscriptions settings
LinkedIn cannot provide billing support for iTunes purchases — refunds must go through Apple
refundBasis: LinkedIn Premium subscriptions may be refunded within 7 days of being charged if unused; EU subscribers get a 14-day right, and Denmark/Netherlands residents get a prorated refund on cancellation.

name: Match
cancelSteps: Sign in and click the gear/settings icon
Select Manage Subscription
Follow the prompts to cancel (turns off auto-renewal)
If subscribed via Apple, cancel through Apple's Subscriptions settings instead
traps: Cancelling turns off auto-renewal but does not refund the current period
refundBasis: Match's Terms of Use make subscriptions non-refundable, with an exception only if the user dies or becomes disabled before the subscription ends.

name: Tinder
cancelSteps: Tinder subscriptions are billed by Apple or Google, not Tinder directly — open the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android) app
On Google Play: Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions > Tinder Gold > Cancel subscription
On Apple: Settings > your name > Subscriptions > Tinder Gold/Platinum > Cancel Subscription
traps: Uninstalling the app does not cancel the subscription
Refunds are handled entirely by Apple or Google, not Tinder
refundBasis: Tinder defers all refund decisions to Apple's or Google's own policies and does not publish its own refund terms.

name: Bumble
cancelSteps: If purchased directly from Bumble: open payment settings under your profile and cancel there
If purchased via Apple App Store or Google Play: cancel through that store's subscription settings instead
Cancel at least 24 hours before renewal to avoid another charge
refundBasis: Bumble does not give prorated refunds on cancellation; California subscribers can cancel and get a refund within 3 business days of subscribing, and Apple/Google purchases follow their own refund rules.

name: Planet Fitness
cancelSteps: Planet Fitness does not accept cancellation online, by phone, by email, or through the app
Visit your home club in person and cancel at the front desk, OR
Mail a signed cancellation letter (name, address, phone, membership ID) via USPS Certified Mail to your home club (not corporate)
traps: Only your original "home club" can process the cancellation — mailing corporate headquarters does not work
No online or app cancellation option exists despite online sign-up being available
refundBasis: Planet Fitness's public customer-service page describes how to cancel but does not state a refund policy for dues already paid.

name: Peloton
cancelSteps: Open the Peloton app (web cancellation is not offered for App membership) and go to Preferences > Memberships
Select Manage next to the subscription, then Cancel Subscription
Choose a cancellation reason and decline any retention offer
Confirm; a confirmation email is sent
traps: If subscribed via Apple or Google Play, their refund policies apply instead of Peloton's
refundBasis: Peloton's Membership Terms say there is no prorated refund for the current membership period, with a narrow exception for New York residents within 14 days of a price increase.

name: SiriusXM
cancelSteps: Contact SiriusXM via chat at siriusxm.com/contactus or call 866-635-8641 to cancel
Confirm the cancellation effective date and keep the chat transcript or confirmation
traps: If purchased through the App Store, Google Play, Roku, or T-Mobile, that platform's refund policy applies instead
refundBasis: SiriusXM audio subscriptions are non-refundable as of March 2024, with limited exceptions: annual plans within 30 days and monthly plans within 7 days.

name: The New York Times
cancelSteps: Sign in at myaccount.nytimes.com
Open Account and Subscription Overview
Select the subscription and complete the cancellation option
Or call Customer Care at (800) 591-9233
refundBasis: The New York Times states no refund or credit is normally due for time remaining after cancellation, except where required by law.

name: The Wall Street Journal
cancelSteps: Sign in at customercenter.wsj.com with your subscription email
Go to Subscriptions / Manage Subscription
Select Cancel subscription and follow the prompts
Or call 1-800-JOURNAL (568-7625)
refundBasis: WSJ's customer center provides cancellation steps but no published refund policy was found on its own help pages.

name: Duolingo
cancelSteps: Sign in on duolingo.com or the app
Open account/subscription settings and select cancel Super Duolingo
If billed via Apple or Google, cancel through that app store instead
refundBasis: Duolingo's help center states cancelling will not retroactively refund subscription payments and fees are not prorated by cancellation date.

name: Grammarly
cancelSteps: Sign in at account.grammarly.com
Click Account tab, then Your account > Subscription
Click Cancel Subscription at the bottom of the page
Click Continue to confirm
If purchased via Apple or Google Play, cancel through that app store instead
refundBasis: Grammarly says refunds are issued only if required by law; it operates a strict non-refundable policy for all subscription plans.

name: Canva
cancelSteps: Sign in and open Menu > Settings > Billing & Plans
Select Cancel subscription and confirm
If subscribed via Apple or Google, cancel through that app store instead
refundBasis: Canva gives a full refund if you cancel within 30 days of purchasing a yearly plan; monthly plans are generally not refunded once billed.

name: Chegg
cancelSteps: Sign in and go to My Account > Orders
Open the Subscriptions tab, select the plan and click Continue
Choose a cancellation reason and click Continue
Click the Cancel Subscription button to confirm
traps: Must be done from a laptop/desktop browser to permanently cancel, per Chegg's own guidance
refundBasis: No standard refund policy was found on Chegg's own help pages; refunds for unused tutoring minutes are handled case-by-case through customer service.

name: Uber One
cancelSteps: Open the Uber or Uber Eats app (no separate web cancel page)
Go to Account, select Uber One
Select Manage Membership, then End Membership
traps: Cancel at least 24-48 hours before the renewal date to avoid another charge
After a refund, you can't repurchase Uber One for 3 days
refundBasis: Uber states Uber One payments are non-refundable and not prorated, except that a charge within 24 hours of cancelling before renewal is automatically refunded.

name: DoorDash DashPass
cancelSteps: Sign in on the DoorDash app or doordash.com
Go to Account > Manage DashPass
Select Cancel Membership, choose a reason, and submit
traps: Must cancel at least 24 hours before the next scheduled payment to avoid another charge
refundBasis: DoorDash says DashPass does not issue refunds once you cancel, though benefits remain until the end of the current billing period.

name: Instacart+
cancelSteps: Sign in on instacart.com or the app
Select the menu icon (web) or Account icon (app), then Your Instacart+ membership
Under Manage your membership, select Cancel membership
refundBasis: Instacart+ annual members can cancel within the first 5 calendar days and get a full refund if no orders were placed with the membership; monthly plans get no prorated refund.

name: Walmart+
cancelSteps: Sign in at walmart.com and open your account
Select Walmart+, then Manage membership
Select Manage beside your plan, then Cancel beside Cancel membership
Or call Walmart Customer Care at (800) 924-9206
traps: A pause option (up to 1 month at a time, 3x per year) exists as an alternative to full cancellation
refundBasis: Walmart's Terms of Use state the membership fee is non-refundable except as expressly stated or required by law.

name: Costco Membership
cancelSteps: Costco does not offer online cancellation
Cancel in person at the membership desk of any warehouse (refund issued immediately), OR
Call 1-800-774-2678 to cancel by phone (refund lands on original payment method within a few business days)
traps: Online cancellation is not available — only in person or by phone
refundBasis: Costco's 100% satisfaction guarantee lets a member cancel and get a full, non-prorated refund of the membership fee at any time.

name: PlayStation Plus
cancelSteps: Sign in to Account Management (via the link on this page or account.sony.com)
Select Subscription
Select Cancel below the PlayStation Plus subscription
Or on console: Settings > Users and Accounts > Payment and Subscriptions > Subscriptions > PlayStation Plus > Turn Off Auto-Renew
refundBasis: Sony gives a full refund if you cancel within 14 days of purchase and haven't used the benefits; a partial refund based on days remaining applies if you have used it.

name: Nintendo Switch Online
cancelSteps: Sign in at accounts.nintendo.com/portal
Select Nintendo Switch Online
Select Terminate automatic renewal, then confirm
Do this at least 48 hours before expiration
traps: Once auto-renewal is turned off it cannot be turned back on for that membership term
Cloud save backups stop working once the membership lapses (restorable if you resubscribe within 180 days)
refundBasis: Nintendo's terms say it cannot offer refunds or credits for remaining membership time, aside from a statutory 14-day right in some regions outside the US.

name: QuickBooks Online
cancelSteps: Sign in to QuickBooks Online as the primary or company admin
Go to Settings (gear icon), select Subscriptions and billing
In the QuickBooks section select Cancel subscription and follow the on-screen steps
traps: After cancelling you get read-only access to your data for one year, then must resubscribe to see it again
refundBasis: Intuit offers a refund on annual QuickBooks Online subscriptions if cancelled within 60 days of purchase; monthly subscriptions are not eligible for a prorated refund.

name: Restoro
cancelSteps: Log into your Restoro account dashboard
Go to subscription settings and select Cancel Subscription
If the automated flow fails, submit a ticket at restoro.com/submit-ticket or email support@restoro.com
traps: In March 2024 the FTC charged Restoro (with Reimage) with using deceptive fake Windows pop-ups and scan results to scare people into paying for repair services; the companies paid $26 million to settle, and the FTC has been sending consumer refunds since 2025
To get Restoro's own refund you must run its uninstall wizard and choose Revert changes / Revert and remove Restoro before requesting the refund
refundBasis: Restoro's own policy offers a refund within 60 days of purchase, but only after completing its uninstall/revert process and submitting a request through support.

name: Reimage
cancelSteps: No self-service web cancel page was found; licenses renew automatically each year
To cancel, contact support at forwardsupport@reimageplus.com or call 855-432-7277
To request a refund, first uninstall via Add/Remove Programs, choosing Reimage Repair to undo its changes
traps: In March 2024 the FTC charged Reimage (with Restoro) with using deceptive fake Windows pop-ups and scan results to scare people into paying for repair services; the companies paid $26 million to settle, and the FTC has been sending consumer refunds since 2025
refundBasis: Reimage's stated policy honors refund requests within 60 days of purchase or renewal, but requires uninstalling/reverting the program first and contacting support directly.

name: Vercel
notes: Descriptor is just "VERCEL" for the platform plan AND for Vercel Blob/KV usage overage — they land as separate line items but look nearly identical.

name: Vercel Blob (usage add-on)
notes: NOT the same as "VERCEL BLOTO" (Blotato, below) — easy to misread on a statement. Blob is storage inside your Vercel account; Blotato is an unrelated social-scheduling SaaS.

name: Blotato
notes: Social media auto-posting tool. Descriptor sometimes shows through a Vercel-hosted checkout as "VERCEL BLOTO..." — do not confuse with Vercel Blob storage.

name: Supabase
notes: Check the dashboard for paused vs active projects; paused projects still bill on Pro tier after the grace period.

name: Clerk
typicalPriceRange: 0 (up to 10k MAU) / 25+ (Pro, usage-based above included MAU)
notes: Billed per monthly active user above the free tier — a dead app can still show a small charge from stale sessions.

name: Neon (Postgres)
notes: Compute-hour billing — a branch left un-suspended keeps burning hours even with zero application traffic.

name: Railway
notes: Usage-based on top of the base plan fee — a forgotten worker service quietly adds to the usage line even with no traffic.

name: Cloudflare
notes: Most zones are free; a charge usually means a Pro/Business zone plan, Workers paid plan, or R2/D1 usage overage.

name: GitHub
notes: Watch for org-level Copilot Business seats assigned to inactive collaborators — they bill per seat, not per usage.

name: OpenAI API
typicalPriceRange: usage-based, prepaid credit or postpaid invoice
notes: API usage descriptor is distinct from the consumer ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription line below — check both if you have a personal and a project account.

name: X Premium
notes: Personal subscription tier — separate billing surface from the X API tiers. A bare "X.COM" descriptor is AMBIGUOUS: it can be X Premium OR an X API tier — use the amount to tell them apart ($8-40/mo -> Premium; $100+/mo -> API Basic or higher).

name: X API
notes: The classic "forgot I upgraded from Free to Basic" surprise — a $100/mo jump with no warning banner. A bare "X.COM" descriptor is AMBIGUOUS with X Premium (like the OPENAI vs OPENAI *CHATGPT split) — $100+/mo means an API tier, $8-40/mo means Premium.

name: Twilio
typicalPriceRange: ~1.15/mo per US local number + usage-based SMS/voice/verify
notes: A provisioned-but-idle phone number is cheap alone ($1-2/mo) but common to accumulate several across test projects.

name: RunPod
typicalPriceRange: per-second GPU billing, $0.20-$4+/hr depending on GPU class
notes: The single most expensive class of forgotten-resource waste in v1's scope — a left-running GPU pod bills continuously with nothing consuming it.

name: Meshy
notes: 3D asset generation SaaS.

name: Replicate
notes: Per-model, per-second compute billing — a model left warm/pinned can bill even between calls on some plans.

name: Netlify
notes: Common overage: build minutes and bandwidth on abandoned sites still attached to a paid team.

name: Fly.io
notes: Suspended (not destroyed) machines can still hold reserved IPs/volumes that bill.

name: Heroku
notes: Classic forgotten-resource platform — check for apps with zero web traffic still on a paid dyno tier.

name: Render
notes: Paid-tier services don't spin down when idle the way free-tier ones do — that's the trap.

name: DigitalOcean
notes: A stopped (not destroyed) droplet still bills for its reserved disk.

name: Amazon Web Services
typicalPriceRange: highly variable — from single-digit dollars to thousands

name: Microsoft Azure
notes: Same reasoning as AWS — reconcile against Cost Management + Billing.

name: Resend
notes: A verified sending domain left attached after a project sunset is the common forgotten-charge shape here.

name: Groq
notes: Low per-token cost usually means small charges — worth checking a stale key isn't still being called by an old cron.

name: Stripe
typicalPriceRange: processing fees, not a flat subscription (2.9% + 30c typical)
notes: Rarely a "forgotten" charge since it's transaction-linked, but Radar/Billing add-ons and unused Terminal readers can bill flat fees.

name: Notion
notes: Per-seat billing on Business plans is the usual waste vector — check for seats assigned to people who've left.

name: Figma
notes: Editor seats (not viewer seats) are billed — downgrading unused editors to viewers is the quick win.

name: Linear
notes: Per-seat billing — check for seats on workspaces no team actually uses anymore.

name: Slack
notes: Bills per active user monthly — a workspace nobody posts in anymore is a clean cancel.

name: Zoom
notes: Common waste: a Pro host license nobody schedules meetings under anymore (client calls moved to a client's own Zoom).

name: 1Password
notes: Low per-seat cost but easy to accumulate stale seats on a Teams/Business plan.

name: Google Workspace
notes: Per-user billing — check the admin console for suspended/unused mailboxes still on a paid tier.

name: Sentry
notes: Event-volume overage on a project that's been decommissioned is the classic finding here.

name: Datadog
notes: Host-based billing continues even for a host that's been terminated until the agent stops reporting.

name: ElevenLabs
notes: CHECK THE VOICE PATH BEFORE ASSUMING THIS IS NEEDED. SignalWire's AI runtime carries the ElevenLabs voice catalog NATIVELY as a voice string (elevenlabs.<name>:<model>) with no ElevenLabs account, key or vendor relationship — so a phone/voice product can sound like ElevenLabs while paying nothing to them. A paid plan here is only load-bearing for direct TTS/agents in the ElevenLabs workspace itself. Non-use evidence: agents_list returning zero agents plus zero character consumption. Custom/cloned voices do NOT resolve through the SignalWire catalog — that is the one case the paid account is genuinely required.

name: SignalWire
typicalPriceRange: usage-based, funded by top-ups (10 minimum increment); ~0.60-1.00/mo per retained phone number plus per-minute
notes: Balance top-up, not a subscription — a 10.00 charge is the minimum increment, not a plan fee. The recurring cost that hides here is RETAINED PHONE NUMBERS: a number keeps billing monthly after the product it served is retired, and releasing it is the saving.
